subject: Decision criteria: latency, cost, deployment mode & SLA - final clarifications
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@finova.com>, Tom Harwood <tom.harwood@finova.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & final clarifications on decision criteria

Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciate the clarity from your team. Quick recap and the final list of clarifying items we agreed to confirm so your procurement and legal teams have what they need to finish evaluation:

1) Decision criteria (we captured these on the call):
   - Latency target: Finova preference is p95 <= 250ms for 256-token responses; p99 target is softer but ideally < 1s for standard flows.
   - Cost sensitivity: target incremental token cost that keeps cost/unit below your current self-host baseline; you said cost is a gating factor for production scale.
   - Deployment mode: you listed Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) as preferred for predictable throughput, with Private (VPC/on-prem) as a possible requirement for regulated flows.
   - SLA needs: uptime and latency SLOs to be included in contract; redlines in attached SLA draft.

2) Procurement & security steps we discussed:
   - Economic buyer: Tom suggested CFO + Head of Data (please confirm final name).
   - Procurement contact: procurement@finova.com (Tom to confirm primary POC).
   - Legal/security: will run through SOC2 evidence and KMS/HSM options; we shared SOC2 report link and will provide an IP/Architecture diagram if needed.

3) Open technical clarifications we need to finalize pricing/placement:
   - Typical sequence length distribution (50% below 256 tokens?)
   - Expected QPS and burst patterns (diurnal vs batch inference)
   - Any requirements for on-prem or VPC-only data residency for PII flows

Next steps (proposed):
- Tom/Procurement: confirm economic buyer and procurement POC by EOD Fri 11/06.
- Finova: share representative sample of sequence length distribution (or py/prometheus export) so we can run a cost/latency model.
- Redwood: we will update the SLA draft (attached) with your suggested p95/p99 targets and produce a high-level cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private by Mon 11/09.

Attachments: finova-stakeholder-map.xlsx, redwood-sla-draft.pdf

If anything above is off, flag it — otherwise we'll assume this is the plan and follow up with the updated SLA + cost delta next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & final clarifications on decision criteria

On Thu, Nov 5, 2026 at 9:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the time this morning — appreciate the clarity from your team. Quick recap and the final list of clarifying items we agreed to confirm so your procurement and legal teams have what they need to finish evaluation:

Thanks Marissa — this aligns with our notes. A few items to clarify from our side:

- Economic buyer: Confirmed — Laura Bennett (CFO) is the economic buyer for this project. I'll introduce Laura next week in the procurement thread.
- Procurement POC: procurement@finova.com is the right address; primary POC is me (Tom). I'll loop Legal (legal@finova.com) once we have an initial SLA.
- Latency: correct on the p95 <= 250ms target for core flows. For p99 we'll accept up to 1s for synchronous requests, but anything above that will need fallback strategies.
- Deployment mode: we prefer Redwood Dedicated for the first phase. Private/VPC may be required for specific payment-card flows in phase 2.

Attached: finova-procurement-timeline.docx (high-level procurement milestones). We expect procurement timeline to be ~6-8 weeks after final SLA/pricing sign-off.

Tom
VP, Product Operations
Finova
Tom.Harwood@finova.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Harwood <tom.harwood@finova.com>, Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@finova.com>
Cc: dev.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & final clarifications on decision criteria

Thanks Tom + Marissa. A couple of technical clarifications to make the cost/latency estimate accurate:

- Sequence distribution: if you can share percentiles (p50/p90/p95) or a histogram, we will model batching and KV-cache hit rates. Rough rule of thumb: for Dedicated on A100-equivalent, p95 of 250ms for 256 tokens is achievable with continuous batching and prefix caching if QPS is <= 120 and median sequence length is <= 180 tokens.
- SLA metrics: we can draft latency SLO language that ties p95/p99 to specific routes (e.g., interactive chat vs background summarization) and include credits for downtime; see attached SLA draft for proposed language.
- Deployment mode cost delta: high-level guidance — Dedicated (reserved) will have ~25-35% lower unit cost vs Private (VPC/on-prem) once utilization exceeds 60%. We'll provide a precise per-1M-token delta after we see your sequence/QPS distribution.

Action items from Redwood (Rishi/Dev):
- Produce two line-item estimates (Dedicated vs Private) by EOD Mon 11/09.
- Update SLA draft to reflect p95/p99 buckets + proposed credit schedule (attached).
- Offer a 60-day pilot at preferential committed rate if Finova wants to validate latency/cost in-prod.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through the numbers — proposing Tue 11/10 10:00am PT.

-rishi
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Thanks all — this looks good and thanks for the clear next steps. A few quick confirmations:
- Laura (CFO) is the economic buyer; Tom will intro early next week.
- Procurement timeline looks fine (6-8 weeks).
- We accept the proposed p95/p99 buckets; small ask from Legal: include explicit data residency clause for payment-card-related flows (we'll provide wording).
- We'd like the Dedicated vs Private cost estimates and the 60-day pilot pricing before Tue 11/10 call.

I'll loop Legal and Procurement on any SLA redlines; otherwise we can use the attached SLA draft as the baseline. Please send the cost estimates and I'll confirm the Tue slot once Tom confirms with Laura.

Regards,
Sarah Lin
